SourceActivities: 19.2 adjacent-angle bisectors conjecture and 90 degree proof

Task.Prompt: Label original paper intersecting-line diagram and write a complete narrative proof that vertical angles agree, using a 180-degree rotation or linear-pair equations. Independently prove why the bisectors of two adjacent supplementary angles are perpendicular, then refute a false adjacent-angle claim.

Criteria.Criterion: labels intersecting lines, vertical and supplementary pairs precisely
forms a valid general conjecture and derives the adjacent-bisector 90-degree result
presents an uninterrupted narrative half-turn or supplements proof of vertical equality
critiques an invalid adjacent-angle claim and explains why empirical measurements are insufficient

Items.Prompt: Intersecting straight lines give angle AOB=70 degrees. Determine opposite and adjacent measures.
Items.Expected: Opposite COD=70°, adjacent BOC/DOA=110° by equal supplements.

Items.Prompt: Adjacent angle bisectors split α and β, α+β=180°. Find their included angle.
Items.Expected: α/2+β/2=90°, always, with bisectors inside adjacent angles.

Items.Prompt: Why does a half-turn of D about intersection B land on opposite ray BA but not necessarily at A?
Items.Expected: Half-turn reverses the ray with radius BD; coincidence with A requires BD=BA.

Items.Prompt: Under rotation of a labelled polygon about D followed by translation DE, why may intermediate labels not be skipped?
Items.Expected: The order affects image locations; each rigid stage must be shown and same mapping retained.

Items.Prompt: How to align congruent labelled quadrilaterals point-by-point?
Items.Expected: Translate a vertex, rotate about its image to align neighbour; reflect if necessary while preserving matches.

Items.Prompt: What supports a congruent triangle point correspondence rather than appearance?
Items.Expected: Same pairwise distances and explicit translation-rotation-reflection mapping.

Items.Prompt: A generic kite has reflection axis AC. What does it imply about the other diagonal BD?
Items.Expected: AC perpendicularly bisects BD and reflection exchanges B,D.

Items.Prompt: Do adjacent angles of 70 and 110 degrees have to be equal?
Items.Expected: No. They are supplementary, whereas opposite vertical angles are equal.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: prove vertical 70-degree pair congruent by half-turn and 110-degree supplementary relation
TeacherPaperHandoff: Student gives labelled geometric diagram and continuous written proof to school teacher. Teacher checks each mathematical inference, scores four 0/1/2 criteria, writes feedback and signs/dates the paper; no automatic grade or online evidence storage claimed.

Cases.CORRECT: two justified linear-pair equations or half-turn general proof
Cases.EQUIVALENT: different correct point names, mirrored construction or valid independent narrative theorem
Cases.WRONG: assert adjacent supplementary angles are necessarily equal
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: measurement or two-column skeleton without explanatory proof
Cases.MALFORMED: undefined O, no opposite rays or invalid degenerate linear pair

StageD.Required: exact GEO lesson-to-school teacher assessment assignment and saved grade/feedback; auth and tenant E2E
